record.name: GraphRareBench
record.domain: Phenotype-driven rare-disease diagnosis benchmark with graph-defined confounders and evidence auditing
record.inputs: Per-case coarsened HPO phenotype query with a fixed full and hard candidate disease pool, graph-defined hard confounders and source-linked evidence bundles
record.outputs: Ranked disease predictions scored by MRR/Hit@k, case-averaged target-over-confounder accuracy, bootstrap and paired-bootstrap intervals, plus tool-trace and evidence-coverage audits
record.notes: Frozen release of 2,365 ontology-derived cases (1,892 train / 236 dev / 237 gene-component-disjoint test) and 18,093 target-confounder pairs, shipped with loader, validator, evaluator, bootstrap and agent-audit utilities and benchmark/audit prompt templates under MIT. Reported baselines mix supervised rankers on a shared 21-feature interface (MRR 0.640-0.740) with tool-using agents instantiated on Agents-A1 (MRR 0.746) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0.718), whose paired MRR difference was not significant while target-evidence coverage differed by 0.561.

name: scBench-Long
reason: The worklist premise ('NO released code/data anywhere') does NOT hold and was checked directly. arXiv:2606.26563 verified via arXiv API and HTML (v1, 2026-06-25, q-bio.GN + cs.AI, not withdrawn); the HTML front matter gives the affiliation the abstract page omits: all five authors are LatchBio, San Francisco, correspondence kenny@latch.bio. GitHub repo latchbio/scbench-long is live, non-fork, Apache-2.0, created 2026-06-22 (three days before the arXiv posting), containing evals/manifest.json plus four eval directories with eval.json + vocabulary.json and 121 files of agent trajectories across anthropic/claude-opus-4-8, openai/gpt-5.5, gemini-3.5-flash, fireworks/glm-5p2 and xai/grok-4.3. Ownership is the authors' own company org (api.github.com/orgs/latchbio -> LatchBio, https://latch.bio, contact@latch.bio), and the eval IDs match the paper's study systems (melanoma sort-gate CD8, cross-species epithelial communication, senescence, TME context), so this is an official release rather than a reconstruction. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the paper never cites the repo, and the repo README describes itself as a 'public subset' - 4 of the 21 evaluations, with no grading/harness code - so this is a partial data release, classified open-data rather than open-source. No name collision in agents_final.json (neither scBench nor scBench-Long is catalogued).

record.name: scBench-Long
record.domain: Long-horizon single-cell biology agent benchmark (recovering published conclusions from raw data)

repo_links.label: GitHub (latchbio/scbench-long, Apache-2.0, public subset of 4 evals + trajectories)

record.inputs: Per-eval task specification with a compact scientific question and raw or near-raw single-cell data (paired scRNA/TCR, RNA+ATAC, single-nucleus RNA-seq, immune repertoires, ortholog maps, ligand-receptor resources), with no prescribed method
record.outputs: Structured claims graded deterministically against controlled answer vocabularies, plus rubric-based trajectory diagnostics and per-run cost/turn metadata
record.notes: 21 evaluations across melanoma tumour-reactive CD8 T cells, CD8 RNA+ATAC regulatory inference, human-monkey chimera development, KRAS-driven lung tumour aging and lethal COVID-19 lung pathology; across 1,068 completed trajectories the strongest model-harness pair (Claude Opus 4.8 with Claude Code) passed 16/63 runs (25.4%, Wilson 95% CI 16.3-37.3), followed by Gemini 3.5 Flash with PI at 14/63. The public GitHub release from the authors' company org covers only 4 of the 21 evals (eval.json + vocabulary.json) plus example trajectories under Apache-2.0; the grading harness and the remaining evals are not released, and the paper itself contains no availability statement.

name: ProtoPilot
reason: arXiv:2606.31763 verified via arXiv API and full HTML (v1 2026-06-30, v2 2026-07-02, cs.AI, not withdrawn). HTML front matter gives affiliations absent from the abstract page: 1 Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, 2 Genoria AI (Shenzhen), corresponding jiangyankai@pjlab.org.cn, wangxiaosong@pjlab.org.cn, bailei@pjlab.org.cn, yangmeng@genoria.ai. I scanned every URL in the v2 HTML: there is no code, data or project link of any kind, and no availability section, so ARTIFACT = none and access is paper-only (legitimate per the rules). GitHub search for 'ProtoPilot' returns only unrelated third-party projects (product-prototyping tools, hackathon repos) - none author-linked, so nothing was attached. Scope: multi-step wet-lab automation agent (intent -> protocol -> SOP -> instrument code -> physical execution -> feedback-guided revision), well inside the lane and comparable to the catalogued AutoLabs entry.

record.name: ProtoPilot
record.domain: Wet-lab protocol generation, instrument-code synthesis and robotic execution for synthetic and molecular biology
record.inputs: Natural-language experimental objective plus laboratory context (available reagents, consumables, instruments) supplied through multi-turn clarification
record.outputs: Validated protocol and SOP layers, SDK-compliant instrument code for MGI AlphaTool, Hamilton STAR, Opentrons OT-2 and Tecan EVO, executed workflows with experimental readouts, and feedback-revised protocol versions
record.notes: Self-evolving multi-agent system with an Orchestrator maintaining workflow state over a five-layer representation (intent, protocol, manual SOP, device SOP, instrument code), rubric-based validators and a runtime-updated skill library; benchmark of 294 tasks from 98 gold-standard protocols gives Top@3 expert preference 90.2%, overall protocol-to-code gate pass 96.6% and Opentrons pass 88.2% vs 32.4% for OpenTrons-AI. Physical closure is real but partial and human-gated: the paper discloses human-in-the-loop checkpoints at which the Orchestrator asks the user to confirm material availability, instrument capability and adjustments, and wet-lab work (96-well inoculation, dilution series, colony PCR, plasmid construction, mutagenesis, PCA assembly with Sanger confirmation) involved off-deck human steps; the paper does not state that the agent triggers instrument runs itself, though it did revise the PCA protocol after wet-lab failures and obtain sequence-confirmed assemblies in the subsequent round.
aliases: A Self-Evolving Agentic System for Automated Generation and Execution of Biological Protocols

The agent layer really is released - pepcraft/ contains Initialization.py, agents/{generating,filtering,verifying}_agent.json, Planner and Executor prompt sets, state classes and tools/{Generating/AMPGAN_v3.py, Filtering/*, Verifying/Verify_DBAASP.py, Verify_SwissProt.py}. record.name: PepCraft
record.domain: Antimicrobial peptide design, filtering and database verification (non-canonical chemistry)
record.inputs: Peptide design objective (target activity class, allowed chemistry including D-amino acids and N/C-terminus modifications) issued to the Planning Agent
record.outputs: Generated peptide sequences, physicochemical and structural filter verdicts, DBAASP/SwissProt novelty checks, and a ranked prioritisation report with executor trajectories
record.notes: Planning Agent orchestrates specialised executors for generation (AMPGAN v3, a two-discriminator conditional GAN covering D-amino acids and terminal modifications), physicochemical/structural filtering and database verification; the released repo carries the agent prompts, agent specs and tool implementations but no licence. Wet-lab closure is human-run and retrospective: five AMPGAN v3 candidates were synthesised and assayed by the authors (two active against Gram-positive strains, best MIC 8 ug/mL against B. subtilis), and PepCraft's prioritisation was compared with those existing outcomes - the paper explicitly calls prospective evaluation of its selection ability future work.

record.name: DeepBD
record.domain: Variant prioritisation and diagnostic interpretation for genetic birth defects
record.inputs: Patient case with candidate variants from exome/genome sequencing plus phenotype descriptions (free text mapped to HPO terms) and heterogeneous evidence sources (population genetics, variant-effect predictors, gene-disease validity, ClinVar/HGMD, pathway and structure context)
record.outputs: Ranked patient-specific candidate variants with provenance-preserving evidence records and a diagnosis-oriented synthesis for clinician review
record.notes: Four-part workflow - LLM-assisted case structuring, a pretrained evidence engine (graph attention over phenotype-conditioned biological context fused with rule and variant-effect evidence), specialist evidence modules, and a grounded agentic review layer doing curation, constrained reranking, provenance audit and synthesis; the central ranking substrate is supervised rather than LLM-driven. Developed on an in-house cohort of 18,622 fetal and infant cases with Recall@1/3/5/10 of 0.658/0.882/0.912/0.929 on an internal held-out solved-case benchmark against Exomiser, DeepRare and prompted LLM reranking. Retrospective and single-institution by the authors' own account; diagnostic synthesis is described as requiring separate expert evaluation, and no code or data are released.

reason: Record verified three ways this session: Crossref for DOI 10.64898/2026.06.24.26356357 (openRxiv/medRxiv, posted 2026-07-01, accepted 2026-08-07, CC BY 4.0, funder award R01HG120566), the medRxiv API via the bioRxiv MCP (corresponding author Cong Liu, Boston Children's Hospital; Harvard Medical School), and NCBI eutils esummary for PMID 42428098 (PMC13345393, DOI matches, last author Chung WK). Not withdrawn; v2 is live on medRxiv. ARTIFACT CHECK, which is the substantive finding: the v2 Data Availability section names 'https://github.com/stormliucong/RESCUE-Agent' as the source code, and that repository returns 404 (both api.github.com and the HTML page) as of 2026-08-13; the other cited repo, stormliucong/RESCUE-n8n, IS live and owned by the corresponding author (GitHub user 'Cong Liu', company 'Boston Children's Hospital') but contains an unrelated patient/PCP/genetic-counsellor chat system - its n8n_local/workflows holds Front_Desk, Education, Schedule, Triage, Admin and Diagnostic agents, none of the paper's Ontology/Modeling/Screening/Review agents - and carries no licence. So no usable artifact: access = paper-only. In scope as a multi-step agentic pipeline (ontology mapping -> PU model building -> population screening -> evidence review) alongside catalogued clinical precedents. No name collision in agents_final.json.

record.name: RESCUE
record.domain: Proactive rare-disease patient screening and genomic-testing escalation across an institutional EHR
record.inputs: Institutional EHR data (diagnosis and test codes, clinical notes) for the full patient population, plus a target rare-disease definition
record.outputs: A four-tier genetic-evidence taxonomy over EHR codes, a trained PU XGBoost case/control classifier, a population-wide ranked candidate list, and per-candidate chart-review judgements on genomic-testing appropriateness
record.notes: Four specialised LLM agents - Ontology (code taxonomy), Modeling (positive-unlabelled XGBoost classifier), Screening (population-wide application) and Review (samples clinical notes to judge medical necessity and feasibility) - run as an end-to-end workflow on data from a pediatric hospital: holdout AUC 0.808 (n=12,591), 175,842 of nearly 500,000 patients met screening inclusion, and flagged candidates were 7.4-fold more likely to receive subsequent genomic assessment. Human gates are disclosed and load-bearing: blinded manual chart review by a study author established the 80% precision figure, and the workflow escalates candidates for clinician decision rather than ordering tests. The v2 Data Availability statement points at github.com/stormliucong/RESCUE-Agent, which did not exist when checked on 2026-08-13.
aliases: Rare Disease Detection and Escalation Support via a Learning Health System
